hints.title: Negative Base Division Invariant
hints.text: In negabinary base -2, each digit must be 0 or 1. Use the division identity n = (-2) * q + r, where the remainder r must be non-negative (0 or 1).

hints.title: Negative Remainder Correction
hints.text: If standard integer remainder n % -2 yields a negative value, adjust it by adding 2 to the remainder and incrementing the quotient by 1.

hints.title: Base Case and Digits Reversal
hints.text: Handle n = 0 by immediately returning 0. Collect the corrected remainder bits from least significant to most significant and reverse the accumulated array.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard positive base conversion formulas produce negative digits when the base is negative.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative division with remainder normalization processes one bit per step using minimal string storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle non-negative remainder adjustments in negative radix arithmetic.
complexity.notes: Every integer has a unique representation in negabinary base -2 without needing a sign symbol.
